html:
Muhammad Ali Jinnah was a lawyer and politician, born in Karachi in 1876, who led the All India Muslim League and founded Pakistan. Pakistanis call him Quaid-e-Azam, the great leader.

He trained as a barrister in London. He began in the Indian National Congress and was called an ambassador of Hindu and Muslim unity; he helped make the Lucknow Pact of 1916 between Congress and the League. He left Congress in 1920, disliking Gandhi's mass protest and religious tone.

In the 1930s he rebuilt the League and came to argue that Muslims were a separate nation. The League's Lahore Resolution of 1940 called for independent Muslim states in the northwest and east. Talks with Congress and Britain failed, and in August 1946 his call for "direct action" led to terrible riots in Calcutta.

With the Partition of India in August 1947 he became Pakistan's first governor general. He was already ill with tuberculosis and died in September 1948. His speech of August 1947, promising freedom of religion to all citizens, is still argued over in Pakistan.
